category: Scripting: ReportSetup, FieldsReporter, Solutions, oDesign, oProject & oDesktop Commands
description: The post-processing and housekeeping side of the native object model: ReportSetup commands for traces, output variables, templates and report data, the stack-based FieldsReporter calculator and field-overlay commands, Solutions-module exports (network data, eigenmodes, source editing), and the oDesign / oProject / oDesktop methods for solving, variations, solution types, variables, datasets, design settings, the ChildObject API, directories, registry, autosave, job submission, messages and the ScriptEnv/ScriptArgument entry points of IronPython scripts.

tools.name: oModule("ReportSetup").CreateReport - report types, display types, context and families arrays
tools.description: The full argument structure of CreateReport: report name, report type ("Modal Solution Data", "Terminal Solution Data", "Eigenmode Parameters", "Fields", "Far Fields", "Near Fields", "Antenna Parameters", "Emission Test"), display type ("Rectangular Plot", "Polar Plot", "Radiation Pattern", "Smith Chart", "Data Table", "3D Rectangular Plot", "3D Polar Plot", "Rectangular Contour Plot", "Rectangular Stacked Plot", "3D Rectangular Bar Plot"), solution, context array (Domain, Context for spheres/polylines/arrays), families array (sweep variable values) and the report data array (X and Y components). The basic call is catalogued with ExportToFile; this entry lists the option vocabulary.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
oModule.CreateReport(<ReportName>, <ReportType>, <DisplayType>, <SolutionName>, <ContextArray>, <FamiliesArray>, <ReportDataArray>, <ExtendedInfo>)
# context examples
["Domain:=", "Sweep"]                                   # frequency-domain S-parameters
["Context:=", "3D"]                                     # far fields on infinite sphere '3D'
["Context:=", "Polyline1", "PointCount:=", 1001]        # fields along a polyline
["Domain:=", "Time", "HoldTime:=", 1, "RiseTime:=", 0, "StepTime:=", 6.25e-12, "Step:=", False, "WindowWidth:=", 1, "WindowType:=", 0, "KaiserParameter:=", 1, "MaximumTime:=", 6.24e-9]   # TDR
# families
["Freq:=", ["All"], "patch_l:=", ["27mm", "29mm"]]
["Freq:=", ["2.45GHz"], "Theta:=", ["All"], "Phi:=", ["0deg", "90deg"]]
# data
["X Component:=", "Freq", "Y Component:=", ["dB(S(1,1))", "dB(S(2,1))"]]
["Theta Component:=", "Theta", "Phi Component:=", "Phi", "Mag Component:=", ["dB(GainTotal)"]]   # 3D polar
["X Component:=", "Freq", "Y Component:=", ["S(1,1)"]]   # Smith chart takes the complex quantity

parameters.name: ReportType
parameters.description: Category; must match the solution type (Modal vs Terminal) and the context (Far Fields need a sphere).

parameters.name: DisplayType
parameters.description: Plot kind; Radiation Pattern and 3D Polar are for angular data, Smith Chart for complex S/Gamma.

parameters.name: SolutionName
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1", "Setup1 : LastAdaptive", "Setup1 : AdaptivePass" (convergence), or "Setup1 : Transient".

parameters.name: ContextArray
parameters.description: Domain and/or Context (sphere name, polyline with PointCount, array/source context, differential pairs, matrix).

parameters.name: FamiliesArray
parameters.description: Sweep variable -> values; the primary sweep variable normally gets ["All"].

parameters.name: ReportDataArray
parameters.description: X Component and Y Component (list), or the Theta/Phi/Mag components for 3D polar plots.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
oModule.CreateReport("Gain 3D", "Far Fields", "3D Polar Plot", "Setup1 : LastAdaptive", ["Context:=", "3D"],
    ["Freq:=", ["2.45GHz"], "Theta:=", ["All"], "Phi:=", ["All"]],
    ["Theta Component:=", "Theta", "Phi Component:=", "Phi", "Mag Component:=", ["dB(GainTotal)"]], [])
oModule.CreateReport("E along probe", "Fields", "Rectangular Plot", "Setup1 : LastAdaptive", ["Context:=", "Probe", "PointCount:=", 1001],
    ["Distance:=", ["All"], "Freq:=", ["2.45GHz"], "Phase:=", ["0deg"]],
    ["X Component:=", "Distance", "Y Component:=", ["Mag_E"]], [])
oModule.CreateReport("Smith", "Modal Solution Data", "Smith Chart", "Setup1 : Sweep1", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"],
    ["Freq:=", ["All"]], ["Polar Component:=", ["S(1,1)"]], [])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.post.create_report(expressions, setup_sweep_name, domain, variations, primary_sweep_variable, secondary_sweep_variable, report_category, plot_type, context). Recording a report from the GUI reveals the exact component key names for each display type (e.g. Polar Component for Smith charts).

tools.name: oModule("ReportSetup").AddTraces / UpdateTraces / DeleteTraces / UpdateReports / UpdateAllReports
tools.description: Trace-level report commands: add traces to an existing report with their own solution, context, families and data arrays, update the definition of existing traces, delete traces by name, and force reports to refresh from the latest solution data (one list of reports, or all). They mirror Modify Report > Add Trace / Update and are used to build multi-solution comparison plots.
tools.usage:
oModule.AddTraces(<ReportName>, <SolutionName>, <ContextArray>, <FamiliesArray>, <ReportDataArray>, [])
oModule.UpdateTraces(<ReportName>, [<TraceNames>], <SolutionName>, <ContextArray>, <FamiliesArray>, <ReportDataArray>, [])
oModule.DeleteTraces([<ReportName>], [<TraceNames>])
oModule.UpdateReports(["XY Plot 1", "XY Plot 4"])
oModule.UpdateAllReports()

parameters.name: TraceNames
parameters.description: As listed in the report's Traces tab, typically the expression plus variation suffix; list them through the ChildObject API (oDesign.GetChildObject("Results").GetChildObject(<plot>).GetChildNames()).

parameters.name: arrays
parameters.description: Same structure as in CreateReport.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
oModule.AddTraces("S11 compare", "Setup2 : Sweep1", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"], ["Freq:=", ["All"]],
    ["X Component:=", "Freq", "Y Component:=", ["dB(S(1,1))"]], [])
oModule.UpdateReports(["S11 compare"])
oModule.UpdateAllReports()
tools.notes: PyAEDT: report.add_trace_to_report / update_trace_in_report / delete_traces, hfss.post.update_report_dynamically. With 'Update reports dynamically on edits' disabled (Tools > Options), UpdateReports is needed after a re-solve before exporting.

tools.name: oModule("ReportSetup").DeleteReports / DeleteAllReports / RenameReport / GetAllReportNames / CopyReportsData / PasteReports / ImportIntoReport
tools.description: Report inventory commands: delete named reports or all reports, rename a report, list report names, copy the data of reports to the clipboard and paste them as static (imported) traces into a design, and import a CSV/TAB/DAT file into an existing report as traces (e.g. measurements over simulation).
tools.usage:
oModule.DeleteReports(["XY Plot 1"])
oModule.DeleteAllReports()
oModule.RenameReport("XY Plot 1", "S11_baseline")
names = oModule.GetAllReportNames()
oModule.CopyReportsData(["Transmission", "Reflection"])
oModule.PasteReports()
oModule.ImportIntoReport("Plot1", "C:/meas/vna.csv")

parameters.name: report names
parameters.description: Names as shown under Results in the project tree.

parameters.name: file for ImportIntoReport
parameters.description: .csv, .tab or .dat with a header row; columns become traces.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
for r in oModule.GetAllReportNames():
    if r.startswith("tmp"):
        oModule.DeleteReports([r])
oModule.CopyReportsData(["S11"])       # freeze before re-solve
oModule.PasteReports()
oModule.ImportIntoReport("S11", "C:/meas/vna_s11.csv")
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.post.delete_report, rename_report, all_report_names, copy_report_data, paste_report_data, report.import_traces. Pasted reports are named with an 'Imported' suffix and are independent of the solution.

tools.name: oModule("ReportSetup").CreateReportFromTemplate / SaveReportAsTemplate / ExportImageToFile / ExportUniformPointsToFile
tools.description: Report templates and exports: create a report from an .rpt template saved earlier (Save As Report Template), save a report as a template, export a report image at a given size, and export report data resampled on a uniform grid. Templates carry expressions, context and formatting, so a validated set of plots can be reproduced on any design with the same port names.
tools.usage:
oModule.CreateReportFromTemplate("C:/MyHFSSProjects/PersonalLib/ReportTemplates/TestTemplate.rpt")
oModule.SaveReportAsTemplate("XY Plot 1", "C:/templates/s_params.rpt")
oModule.ExportImageToFile("XY Plot 1", "C:/work/xy1.png", 1600, 900)
oModule.ExportUniformPointsToFile("XY Plot 1", "C:/work/xy1_uniform.csv", "1GHz", "6GHz", "10MHz", False)

parameters.name: template path
parameters.description: .rpt file; templates saved under PersonalLib/ReportTemplates appear in the Results > Create Report From Template menu.

parameters.name: ExportImageToFile arguments
parameters.description: Report name, file (extension picks the format), width, height in pixels.

parameters.name: ExportUniformPointsToFile arguments
parameters.description: Report, file, start, stop, step, and a flag for trace-number formatting.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
oModule.SaveReportAsTemplate("S params", "C:/templates/sparams.rpt")
# in another design
oModule.CreateReportFromTemplate("C:/templates/sparams.rpt")
oModule.ExportImageToFile("S params", "C:/work/sparams.png", 1920, 1080)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: report.apply_report_template, hfss.post.create_report_from_configuration(".rpt"), export_report_to_jpg, export_report_to_file(uniform=True). Templates reference solution names; when they differ, edit the report's solution afterwards.

tools.name: oModule("OutputVariable").CreateOutputVariable / oDesign.GetOutputVariableValue / DeleteOutputVariable / GetOutputVariables
tools.description: Output variables in the native model: create a named report expression bound to a solution, report type and context, evaluate it for an intrinsic variation from the design, delete it, and list existing ones. Output variables are the quantities Optimetrics goals and other expressions reference by name.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("OutputVariable")
oModule.CreateOutputVariable("PeakGain", "max(dB(GainTotal))", "Setup1 : LastAdaptive", "Far Fields", ["Context:=", "3D", "Domain:=", "Sweep"])
oModule.CreateOutputVariable("RL", "dB(S(1,1))", "Setup1 : Sweep1", "Modal Solution Data", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"])
val = oDesign.GetOutputVariableValue("RL", "Freq='2.45GHz'", "Setup1 : Sweep1", "Modal Solution Data", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"])
oModule.DeleteOutputVariable("RL")
names = oModule.GetOutputVariables()

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: Any report expression valid for the report type.

parameters.name: solution / report type / context
parameters.description: As in CreateReport; far-field expressions need the sphere context.

parameters.name: intrinsic variation (GetOutputVariableValue)
parameters.description: "Freq='2.45GHz' Theta='0deg' Phi='0deg'" style string fixing the intrinsics; returns a double.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("OutputVariable")
oModule.CreateOutputVariable("RL_2p45", "dB(S(1,1))", "Setup1 : Sweep1", "Modal Solution Data", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"])
oDesign.Analyze("Setup1")
rl = oDesign.GetOutputVariableValue("RL_2p45", "Freq='2.45GHz'", "Setup1 : Sweep1", "Modal Solution Data", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"])
oDesktop.AddMessage(oProject.GetName(), oDesign.GetName(), 0, "RL at 2.45 GHz = %.2f dB" % rl)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.create_output_variable / get_output_variable / output_variables. In older releases CreateOutputVariable lives on the ReportSetup module; the OutputVariable module is the current location.

tools.name: oModule("ReportSetup").ChangeProperty (report formatting: axes, legend, traces, markers, limit lines)
tools.description: Report appearance is edited with ChangeProperty on the ReportSetup module using tab names such as Axis, Legend, Trace, General, Header, Grid and Marker with PropServers like "<plot>:AxisX", "<plot>:AxisY1", "<plot>:Legend", "<plot>:<trace name>" or "<plot>:Header". Everything the Properties window of a report offers (scaling, fonts, labels, colours, line styles, symbol markers, log axes) is reachable this way.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
oModule.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Axis", ["NAME:PropServers", "S11:AxisY1"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Auto Scale", "Value:=", False], ["NAME:Min", "Value:=", "-40"], ["NAME:Max", "Value:=", "0"], ["NAME:Name", "Value:=", "S-parameters (dB)"]]]])
oModule.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Axis", ["NAME:PropServers", "S11:AxisX"], ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Axis Scaling", "Value:=", "Log"], ["NAME:Auto Units", "Value:=", False], ["NAME:Units", "Value:=", "GHz"]]]])
oModule.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Legend", ["NAME:PropServers", "S11:Legend"], ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Show Variation Key", "Value:=", False], ["NAME:Show Solution Name", "Value:=", False]]]])
oModule.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Trace", ["NAME:PropServers", "S11:dB(S(1,1)):Curve1"], ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Line Width", "Value:=", 3], ["NAME:Color", "R:=", 255, "G:=", 0, "B:=", 0], ["NAME:Line Style", "Value:=", "Dash"]]]])

parameters.name: tab
parameters.description: "Axis", "Legend", "Trace", "General", "Header", "Grid", "Marker", "Cartesian Limit Line", "Note".

parameters.name: PropServers
parameters.description: "<plot>:AxisX", "<plot>:AxisY1" (Y2..), "<plot>:Legend", "<plot>:<trace>:Curve1", "<plot>:Header", "<plot>:Grid".

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: GUI labels: Auto Scale, Min, Max, Axis Scaling (Linear/Log), Name, Units, Text Font, Line Width, Line Style, Color, Symbol Style, Show Trace Name ...

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup")
plot = "S params"
oModule.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Axis", ["NAME:PropServers", plot + ":AxisY1"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Auto Scale", "Value:=", False], ["NAME:Min", "Value:=", "-50"], ["NAME:Max", "Value:=", "0"]]]])
oModule.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:General", ["NAME:PropServers", plot + ":General"],
    ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:Back Color", "R:=", 255, "G:=", 255, "B:=", 255]]]])
oModule.ExportImageToFile(plot, "C:/work/sparams.png", 1600, 900)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: report.edit_x_axis / edit_y_axis / edit_x_axis_scaling / edit_y_axis_scaling / edit_grid / edit_legend / edit_general_settings / edit_header. Trace PropServer names include the trace's internal name; record a colour change once to see them.

tools.name: oModule("Solutions").EditSources (post-processing source magnitudes, phases, field type)
tools.description: Set excitation weights for post-processing: a first sub-array with the non-source settings (FieldType Scattered/Incident/Total for incident waves, UseIncidentVoltage, IncludePortPostProcessing, SpecifySystemPower with the power value) followed by one sub-array per source with its name ("Port:mode" in Modal, terminal name in Terminal, incident wave name) and magnitude/phase (plus Terminated flag in Terminal designs). Field plots, far fields and antenna parameters use these weights without re-solving.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Solutions")
oModule.EditSources([
    ["FieldType:=", "ScatteredFields", "UseIncidentVoltage:=", False, "IncludePortPostProcessing:=", True, "SpecifySystemPower:=", False],
    ["Name:=", "P1:1", "Magnitude:=", "1W", "Phase:=", "0deg"],
    ["Name:=", "P2:1", "Magnitude:=", "1W", "Phase:=", "90deg"],
    ["Name:=", "IncPWave1", "Magnitude:=", "1V_per_meter", "Phase:=", "0deg"]])
# Terminal design entries
["Name:=", "Trace_T1", "Terminated:=", False, "Magnitude:=", "1V", "Phase:=", "0deg"]

parameters.name: FieldType
parameters.description: "ScatteredFields", "IncidentFields" or "TotalFields" when incident waves exist.

parameters.name: IncludePortPostProcessing
parameters.description: Apply renormalisation/de-embedding in the weighting.

parameters.name: SpecifySystemPower / SystemPower
parameters.description: Reference power for gain instead of maximum available power.

parameters.name: Magnitude
parameters.description: W for port power, V for incident voltage/terminal, V_per_meter for plane waves, A_per_meter for magnetic sources.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Solutions")
sources = [["FieldType:=", "TotalFields", "UseIncidentVoltage:=", False, "IncludePortPostProcessing:=", True, "SpecifySystemPower:=", False]]
for i in range(4):
    sources.append(["Name:=", "P%d:1" % (i + 1), "Magnitude:=", "1W", "Phase:=", "%ddeg" % (90 * i)])
oModule.EditSources(sources)
oDesign.GetModule("FieldsReporter").UpdateAllFieldsPlots()
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.edit_sources(dict, include_port_post_processing, max_available_power, use_incident_voltage, incident_wave). Every source must be listed; omitted ones keep their previous values only in some releases - list all to be safe.

tools.name: oModule("Solutions").ExportNetworkData (Touchstone / CSV / MATLAB / CITI network export)
tools.description: Export S/Y/Z network data of solved setups/sweeps: design variation key, solution selection array, file format code (2 tab-delimited spreadsheet, 3 Touchstone .sNp, 4 CITIfile, 7 MATLAB .m, 8 terminal Z0 spreadsheet), output file, frequencies ("all" or a list), renormalisation flag and impedance, matrix type ("S"/"Y"/"Z"), and trailing options for precision, format (MA/RI/DB) and comments. It is the native routine behind hfss.export_touchstone.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Solutions")
oModule.ExportNetworkData(<DesignVariationKey>, [<"Setup:Sweep">], <FileFormat>, <OutFile>, <FreqsArray>, <DoRenorm>, <RenormImped>, <DataType>, <Pass>, <ComplexFormat>, <Precision>, <IncludeGammaImped>, <SupportNonStandardExt>, <ExportDirectionalMatrix?>)
oModule.ExportNetworkData("", ["Setup1:Sweep1"], 3, "C:/work/filter.s2p", ["all"], True, 50, "S", -1, 0, 15, True, True, True)

parameters.name: DesignVariationKey
parameters.description: "" for the nominal variation or "patch_l='29mm' patch_w='38mm'".

parameters.name: solution array
parameters.description: ["Setup1:Sweep1"] (note: no spaces around the colon in this command).

parameters.name: FileFormat
parameters.description: 2 = .tab, 3 = Touchstone, 4 = CITI, 7 = MATLAB .m, 8 = terminal Z0 table.

parameters.name: FreqsArray
parameters.description: ["all"] or explicit frequencies with units.

parameters.name: DoRenorm / RenormImped
parameters.description: Renormalise to a real impedance (Touchstone only).

parameters.name: DataType / Pass / ComplexFormat / Precision
parameters.description: "S"/"Y"/"Z"; -1 for the final pass; 0 = MA, 1 = RI, 2 = DB; significant digits.

parameters.name: IncludeGammaImped / SupportNonStandardExt
parameters.description: Write gamma/impedance comments; allow non-standard extensions for mixed impedances.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Solutions")
for l in ["27mm", "29mm", "31mm"]:
    oModule.ExportNetworkData("patch_l='%s'" % l, ["Setup1:Sweep1"], 3, "C:/work/patch_%s.s1p" % l, ["all"], True, 50, "S", -1, 0, 15, True, True, True)
oModule.ExportNetworkData("", ["Setup1:Sweep1"], 2, "C:/work/filter_S.tab", ["all"], False, 50, "S", -1, 0, 15, True, True, True)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.export_touchstone(setup, sweep, output_file, variations, variations_value, renormalization, impedance, gamma_impedance_comments) and hfss.export_results. The trailing argument list grew over releases; extra trailing booleans are ignored by older versions.

tools.name: oModule("Solutions").ExportEigenmodes / ListVariations / GetValidISolutionList / ExportTransientData
tools.description: Other Solutions-module commands: export the eigenmode table (frequency, Q per mode) for a solution and variation to a tab-delimited .eig file, list solved variations of a solution, query which solutions carry data (GetValidISolutionList), and export transient port signals. Together with ExportNetworkData they cover Results > Solution Data exports.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Solutions")
oModule.ExportEigenmodes("Setup1 : LastAdaptive", "", "C:/mydir/myeigenmode.eig")
variations = oModule.ListVariations("Setup1 : Sweep1")
valid = oModule.GetValidISolutionList()
oModule.ExportTransientData("Setup1 : Transient", "", "C:/work/transient.csv")

parameters.name: solution
parameters.description: "Setup : LastAdaptive" (eigenmodes) or "Setup : Sweep".

parameters.name: variation
parameters.description: Variation key string or empty for nominal.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Output path; .eig is a tab-delimited text table.

tools.example:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Solutions")
for v in oModule.ListVariations("Modes : LastAdaptive"):
    safe = v.replace("'", "").replace("=", "_").replace(" ", "_") or "nominal"
    oModule.ExportEigenmodes("Modes : LastAdaptive", v, "C:/work/modes_%s.eig" % safe)
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.create_q_factor_report exports the Q table; hfss.available_variations.variations wraps ListVariations. ExportEigenmodes is unavailable for HFSS-IE designs; the exact spelling of the valid-solution query varies by release - check the scripting guide of the installed version.

tools.name: oModule("FieldsReporter").EnterVol / EnterSurf / EnterLine / EnterPoint / EnterScalar / EnterVector / EnterComplex / EnterScalarFunc
tools.description: Push operands onto the Fields Calculator stack: geometry (a volume object, a surface/sheet or face list, a polyline, a point object) for integrations and value extraction, and constants (real scalar, vector, complex) or scalar functions (design variables, coordinate functions like X, Y, Z, Phase) for arithmetic with field quantities. They complement EnterQty (field quantities) and CalcOp (operations) already catalogued.
tools.usage:
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("FieldsReporter")
oModule.EnterVol("Box1")
oModule.EnterSurf("Sheet1")            # object, face-list or a named selection
oModule.EnterLine("Polyline1")
oModule.EnterPoint("Point1")
oModule.EnterScalar(3.14159265358979)
oModule.EnterVector(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
oModule.EnterComplex(1.0, 0.5)
oModule.EnterScalarFunc("Phase")       # or a variable name such as "patch_w"

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Object / list / polyline / point name as in the modeler.

parameters.name: scalar / vector / complex values
parameters.description: Numbers in SI units.

parameters.name: EnterScalarFunc
parameters.description: Function name: X, Y, Z, Phase, Freq, Time, Distance, or any design variable.

tools.example:
ofr = oDesign.GetModule("FieldsReporter")
ofr.CalcStack("clear")
# voltage along a line: integrate E dot tangent along Polyline1
ofr.EnterQty("E"); ofr.CalcOp("Real"); ofr.CalcOp("Tangent"); ofr.CalcOp("Dot")
ofr.EnterLine("VLine"); ofr.CalcOp("LineValue"); ofr.CalcOp("Integrate")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("V_line", "Fields")
# radiated power through the region surface
ofr.CalcStack("clear")
ofr.EnterQty("Poynting"); ofr.CalcOp("Real"); ofr.EnterSurf("Region"); ofr.CalcOp("Normal"); ofr.CalcOp("Integrate")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("Prad", "Fields")
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.post.ofieldsreporter for raw access, hfss.post.fields_calculator.add_expression for catalogued expressions. The calculator is stateful - clear the stack at the start of each sequence and keep the operand order the GUI would use.

tools.name: oModule("FieldsReporter").CalcOp operation names (Mag, ComplexMag, Real, Imag, Phase, Conj, Dot, Cross, Normal, Tangent, Integrate, Maximum, Minimum, Mean, Value, dB, Grad, Div, Curl, Smooth, ...)
tools.description: The operation vocabulary accepted by CalcOp, matching the Fields Calculator buttons: scalar/complex functions (Mag, ComplexMag, Real, Imag, Phase, Conj, Smooth, dB, Abs, Sqrt, Pow, Exp, Ln, Log, Sin/Cos/Tan, Asin..., 1/x, +, -, *, /), vector operations (Dot, Cross, Normal, Tangent, ScalarX/Y/Z, VecX/Y/Z, Grad, Div, Curl, Unit Vec), geometry evaluators (Value, LineValue, SurfaceValue, VolumeValue, Integrate, Maximum, Minimum, Mean, MaxPos, MinPos), and context operations (AtPhase, AtTime, Domain, Derivative). Each consumes the top stack entries and pushes the result.
tools.usage:
oModule.CalcOp("<operation>")
# common sequences
EnterQty("E"); CalcOp("ComplexMag")                                  # |E|
EnterQty("E"); CalcOp("Mag"); EnterVol("Sub"); CalcOp("Maximum")    # max |E| in an object
EnterQty("Poynting"); CalcOp("Real"); EnterSurf("S"); CalcOp("Normal"); CalcOp("Integrate")   # power through S
EnterQty("E"); CalcOp("Real"); CalcOp("Tangent"); CalcOp("Dot"); EnterLine("L"); CalcOp("LineValue"); CalcOp("Integrate")   # voltage
EnterQty("H"); CalcOp("Real"); CalcOp("Tangent"); CalcOp("Dot"); EnterLine("Loop"); CalcOp("LineValue"); CalcOp("Integrate")  # current
EnterQty("Ohmic_Loss"); EnterVol("Conductor"); CalcOp("Integrate")    # volume loss
EnterQty("E"); CalcOp("Mag"); EnterScalar(2); CalcOp("Pow")           # |E|^2

parameters.name: Scalar functions
parameters.description: Mag, ComplexMag, Real, Imag, Phase, Conj, Smooth, dB, Abs, Sqrt, Pow, Exp, Ln, Log, Sin, Cos, Tan, Asin, Acos, Atan, Atan2, 1/x, Neg, +, -, *, /, Max, Min (pairwise).

parameters.name: Vector functions
parameters.description: Dot, Cross, Normal, Tangent, ScalarX, ScalarY, ScalarZ, VecX, VecY, VecZ, Vec, Grad, Div, Curl, Unit Vec, Matl (material property scaling), XForm.

parameters.name: Geometry / output
parameters.description: Value, LineValue, SurfaceValue, VolumeValue, PointValue, Integrate, Maximum, Minimum, Mean, MaxPos, MinPos, Export.

parameters.name: Context
parameters.description: AtPhase, AtTime, Domain (restrict to a region), Derivative, Time Average (via Smooth/AtPhase combinations).

tools.example:
ofr = oDesign.GetModule("FieldsReporter")
ofr.CalcStack("clear")
ofr.EnterQty("E"); ofr.CalcOp("ComplexMag"); ofr.EnterScalar(2); ofr.CalcOp("Pow")
ofr.EnterScalar(8.854e-12)
ofr.CalcOp("*"); ofr.EnterScalar(0.25); ofr.CalcOp("*")          # time-averaged electric energy density (vacuum permittivity)
ofr.EnterVol("Cavity"); ofr.CalcOp("Integrate")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("We_cavity", "Fields")
print(ofr.GetTopEntryValue("Modes : LastAdaptive", ["Freq:=", "2GHz", "Phase:=", "0deg"]))

import ScriptEnv
ScriptEnv.Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop")
oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject()
for d in oProject.GetTopDesignList():
    oDesign = oProject.SetActiveDesign(d)
    print(d, oDesign.GetDesignType())
    if oDesign.GetDesignType() == "HFSS":
        oDesign.AnalyzeAll()
oProject.Save()
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.analyze / analyze_setup / stop_simulations / rename_design / design_type. AnalyzeDistributed uses the machine list of the active distributed configuration; -batchoptions override it for command-line runs.

tools.name: oProject.CopyDesign / Paste / DeleteDesign / GetActiveDesign / GetTopDesignList / Save / Close / GetPath / GetName
tools.description: Project-level design and file management: copy a design and paste it (duplicate, also across open projects), delete a design, get the active design object, list top-level designs, save or close the project and read its path and name. These complement InsertDesign / SetActiveDesign / SaveAs already catalogued.
tools.usage:
oProject.CopyDesign("HFSSDesign1")
new_design = oProject.Paste()          # returns the pasted design object in recent releases
oProject.DeleteDesign("Scratch")
oDesign = oProject.GetActiveDesign()
names = oProject.GetTopDesignList()
oProject.Save()
oProject.Close()
path = oProject.GetPath(); name = oProject.GetName()
oProject.GetDesign("Patch")

parameters.name: design name
parameters.description: Exact design name; Paste creates "<name>1" style unique names.

parameters.name: Close
parameters.description: Closes without saving unless Save was called; oDesktop.CloseProject(name) is the alternative.

tools.example:
oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject()
oProject.CopyDesign("Patch")
oProject.Paste()
copy_name = [d for d in oProject.GetTopDesignList() if d.startswith("Patch") and d != "Patch"][-1]
oProject.SetActiveDesign(copy_name).RenameDesignInstance(copy_name, "Patch_v2")
oProject.Save()
print(oProject.GetPath(), oProject.GetName())
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.duplicate_design, delete_design, design_list, save_project, close_project, project_path/project_name. Cross-project paste: CopyDesign in the source project object, Paste in the target project object.

tools.name: oProject.AddDataset / EditDataset / DeleteDataset / ImportDataset / ExportDataset (oDesign variants for design datasets)
tools.description: Dataset commands: add a dataset from coordinate arrays (project datasets on oProject with $ names, design datasets on oDesign), edit it in place under a possibly new name, delete it, import from a tab-delimited file and export to a file. Datasets feed pwl(dataset, x) expressions, frequency-dependent material properties and thermal modifiers.
tools.usage:
oProject.AddDataset(["NAME:$er_fr4", ["NAME:Coordinates", ["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", 1, "Y:=", 4.4], ["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", 2, "Y:=", 4.35], ["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", 4, "Y:=", 4.3]]])
oProject.EditDataset("$er_fr4", ["NAME:$er_fr4", ["NAME:Coordinates", ["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", 1, "Y:=", 4.5], ["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", 4, "Y:=", 4.3]]])
oProject.DeleteDataset("$er_fr4")
oProject.ImportDataset("C:/data/er.tab")
oProject.ExportDataset("$er_fr4", "C:/data/er_export.tab")
oDesign.AddDataset(["NAME:ds1", ["NAME:Coordinates", ...]])   # design dataset (no $)

parameters.name: Coordinates
parameters.description: List of ["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", x, "Y:=", y] points (3D datasets add "Z:=" and "V:=").

parameters.name: ImportDataset file
parameters.description: Tab- or comma-separated columns; the file name becomes the dataset name.

tools.example:
pts = [(1, 4.4), (2, 4.35), (4, 4.3), (8, 4.22), (12, 4.15)]
coords = ["NAME:Coordinates"] + [["NAME:Coordinate", "X:=", x, "Y:=", y] for x, y in pts]
oProject.AddDataset(["NAME:$er_fr4", coords])
oDesign.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:LocalVariableTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "LocalVariables"],
    ["NAME:NewProps", ["NAME:er_f0", "PropType:=", "VariableProp", "UserDef:=", True, "Value:=", "pwl($er_fr4, 2.45)"]]]])
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.create_dataset / create_dataset1d_project / import_dataset1d, DataSet.update()/delete(). Dataset X values carry no units in the arrays - units are implied by how pwl() is used (here GHz because the expression passes 2.45).

tools.name: oDesktop.EnableAutoSave / CloseAllWindows / ClearMessages / GetMessages / PauseScript / QuitApplication
tools.description: Desktop-level session control: toggle autosave, close all document windows, clear or read the Message Manager (per project/design and severity), pause the script with a dialog until the user clicks OK, and quit the application (releasing licenses). The messages functions are how a script checks for solver errors after Analyze in a headless run.
tools.usage:
oDesktop.EnableAutoSave(False)
oDesktop.CloseAllWindows()
oDesktop.ClearMessages("", "", 3)              # (project, design, severity level to clear up to)
msgs = oDesktop.GetMessages("", "", 0)          # (project, design, minimum severity) -> list of strings
oDesktop.PauseScript("Check the model, then click OK")
oDesktop.QuitApplication()

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: 0 info, 1 warning, 2 error, 3 fatal; ClearMessages clears messages up to the given level, GetMessages returns messages at or above it.

parameters.name: project / design
parameters.description: Names or "" for all/global.

tools.example:
oDesktop.EnableAutoSave(False)
oDesign.Analyze("Setup1")
errors = [m for m in oDesktop.GetMessages(oProject.GetName(), oDesign.GetName(), 2)]
if errors:
    for e in errors: print(e)
    oDesktop.AddMessage(oProject.GetName(), oDesign.GetName(), 1, "solve produced errors")
oProject.Save()
oDesktop.QuitApplication()
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.autosave_disable, hfss.logger.messages / clear_messages, hfss.close_desktop / release_desktop. PauseScript waits for a dialog and therefore must not be used in -ng batch scripts.

tools.name: oDesktop.GetVersion / GetExeDir / GetLibraryDirectory / GetPersonalLibDirectory / GetUserLibDirectory / GetTempDirectory / GetProjectDirectory / SetProjectDirectory
tools.description: Environment queries on the desktop: the AEDT version string, installation and library directories (SysLib, UserLib, PersonalLib), the temporary directory and the default project directory (settable). Scripts use them to locate material libraries, UDPs and report templates, and to write results next to the installation-independent project folder.
tools.usage:
ver = oDesktop.GetVersion()                 # e.g. "2025.1"
exe = oDesktop.GetExeDir()
syslib = oDesktop.GetLibraryDirectory()
personal = oDesktop.GetPersonalLibDirectory()
userlib = oDesktop.GetUserLibDirectory()
tmp = oDesktop.GetTempDirectory()
projdir = oDesktop.GetProjectDirectory()
oDesktop.SetProjectDirectory("D:/aedt_projects")

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: Strings; directory paths use the platform separator.

tools.example:
import os
print(oDesktop.GetVersion(), oDesktop.GetExeDir())
template = os.path.join(oDesktop.GetPersonalLibDirectory(), "ReportTemplates", "sparams.rpt")
if os.path.exists(template):
    oDesign.GetModule("ReportSetup").CreateReportFromTemplate(template)
oDesktop.SetProjectDirectory("D:/aedt_projects")
oProject = oDesktop.NewProject()
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.desktop_class.aedt_version_id / install_path / syslib / userlib / personallib / temp_directory, Desktop.global_project_directory. SetProjectDirectory changes the registry-backed default for new projects.

tools.name: oDesktop.GetRegistryInt / GetRegistryString / SetRegistryInt / SetRegistryString / GetActiveDSOConfigName / SetActiveDSOConfigName / GetDistributedAnalysisEnvironment / SetDistributedAnalysisEnvironment
tools.description: Registry-backed preferences and HPC configuration from a script: read and write integer/string keys under Desktop/... and <Product>/... (the same keys -batchoptions overrides), select the active HPC and Analysis Options configuration for a product by name, and read or set the distributed analysis environment. They let a script configure a session like a batch job before solving.
tools.usage:
num = oDesktop.GetRegistryInt("Desktop/Settings/ProjectOptions/HFSS/UpdateReportsDynamicallyOnEdits")
s = oDesktop.GetRegistryString("Desktop/ProjectDirectory")
oDesktop.SetRegistryInt("Desktop/Settings/ProjectOptions/DoAutoSave", 0)
oDesktop.SetRegistryString("HFSS/HPCLicenseType", "Pool")
cfg = oDesktop.GetActiveDSOConfigName("HFSS")
oDesktop.SetActiveDSOConfigName("HFSS", "Local")
env = oDesktop.GetDistributedAnalysisEnvironment()
oDesktop.SetDistributedAnalysisEnvironment(env)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Full registry path, e.g. "HFSS/NumCoresPerDistributedTask", "HFSS/MPIVendor", "HFSS/EnableGPU", "Desktop/Settings/ProjectOptions/DoAutoSave", "TempDirectory".

parameters.name: product / config name
parameters.description: "HFSS", "HFSS 3D Layout Design", "Maxwell 3D" ... and the name of a saved analysis configuration.

tools.example:
oDesktop.SetRegistryString("HFSS/HPCLicenseType", "Pool")
oDesktop.SetRegistryInt("HFSS/NumCoresPerDistributedTask", 8)
print(oDesktop.GetActiveDSOConfigName("HFSS"))
oDesktop.SetActiveDSOConfigName("HFSS", "Cluster16")
oDesign.AnalyzeDistributed("Setup1")
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.set_registry_key / get_registry_key_string / get_registry_key_int / set_license_type / set_active_dso_config_name / set_registry_from_file. Registry changes persist for the user; prefer -batchoptions for one-off runs.

tools.name: oDesktop.SubmitJob / SelectScheduler / LaunchJobMonitor / RefreshJobMonitor
tools.description: Job submission scripting: choose the scheduler (LSF, PBS, SLURM, UGE, Windows HPC, RSM) and head node, submit a project (or one design/setup) using an .areg settings file exported from the Submit Job dialog, and open/refresh the Job Monitor. SubmitJob returns the job id strings so a script can track the run.
tools.usage:
oDesktop.SelectScheduler("SLURM", "hpc-head", "user", False)      # (scheduler, address, username, forcePasswordEntry) - argument set varies by release
job_ids = oDesktop.SubmitJob("C:/hpc-settings/Submit_Job_Settings.areg", "C:/projects/basic.aedt")
more_ids = oDesktop.SubmitJob("C:/hpc-settings/Submit_Job_Settings.areg", "C:/projects/basic.aedt", "Design1", "Setup1")
oDesktop.LaunchJobMonitor()
oDesktop.RefreshJobMonitor()

parameters.name: settingsPath
parameters.description: .areg file with scheduler, queue, product path, cores/nodes and batch options (Save Settings in the Submit Job dialog).

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: .aedt or .aedtz to solve on the cluster.

parameters.name: design / setup
parameters.description: Optional restriction of the batch solve.

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: Array of job id strings (empty if nothing was submitted).

tools.example:
ids = oDesktop.SubmitJob("C:/hpc/slurm_hfss.areg", oProject.GetPath() + "/" + oProject.GetName() + ".aedt", oDesign.GetName(), "Setup1")
oDesktop.AddMessage(oProject.GetName(), oDesign.GetName(), 0, "submitted jobs: " + ",".join(ids))
oDesktop.LaunchJobMonitor()
tools.notes: PyAEDT: hfss.submit_job(cluster_name, aedt_full_exe_path, nodes, cores, wait_for_license, setting_file), Desktop.select_scheduler / job_status / launch_job_monitor. The scheduler must be configured once in the GUI (Tools > Job Management) so the .areg can be exported.

tools.name: ScriptEnv.Initialize / ScriptEnv.Release / ScriptArgument (IronPython script entry points)
tools.description: The preamble of every IronPython/CPython script run inside AEDT: ScriptEnv.Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop") binds the oDesktop object (and oProject/oDesign when a project is open), ScriptEnv.Release() releases it at the end, and the predefined ScriptArgument variable holds the string passed with -ScriptArgs or the Run Script with Arguments dialog so one script can serve many parameter sets. Scripts run from Tools > Run Script, from the command line with -RunScript / -RunScriptAndExit, or from the IronPython command window.
tools.usage:
import ScriptEnv
ScriptEnv.Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop")
oDesktop.RestoreWindow()
oProject = oDesktop.GetActiveProject()
oDesign = oProject.GetActiveDesign()
oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")
args = ScriptArgument            # string from -ScriptArgs "..." (empty when none)
...
ScriptEnv.Release()

parameters.name: Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop")
parameters.description: Connects to the hosting desktop; in old standalone-IronPython workflows a version string such as "Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop.2025.1" targeted a specific release.

parameters.name: ScriptArgument
parameters.description: Raw argument string; split it yourself (e.g. comma-separated key=value pairs).

parameters.name: Language
parameters.description: AEDT ships IronPython 2.7 for Tools > Run Script; CPython 3.x scripts run through the PyAEDT panels or externally. VBScript uses Set oAnsoftApp = CreateObject("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop").

tools.example:
# sweep.py - run with: ansysedt -RunScriptAndExit sweep.py -ScriptArgs "f0=2.45GHz,passes=12"
import ScriptEnv
ScriptEnv.Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop")
kv = dict(item.split("=") for item in ScriptArgument.split(",")) if ScriptArgument else {}
oProject = oDesktop.OpenProject("C:/work/patch.aedt")
oDesign = oProject.SetActiveDesign("Patch")
oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup")
oModule.EditSetup("Setup1", ["NAME:Setup1", "Frequency:=", kv.get("f0", "2.45GHz"), "MaximumPasses:=", int(kv.get("passes", 10))])
oDesign.Analyze("Setup1")
oProject.Save()
ScriptEnv.Release()
tools.notes: In PyAEDT none of this is needed: from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss; hfss = Hfss() provides hfss.odesktop etc. Recorded scripts always start with the Initialize/RestoreWindow lines; keep them for scripts meant to run under Tools > Run Script.
